consistency_checks.detail: Diagnoses acknowledge uncontrolled BP but no work‑up data (renal labs, renin‑aldosterone) are present to confirm any specific etiology.
Spine‑related diagnoses align with documented axial pain, though imaging is missing.
Medication non‑adherence diagnosis appropriately reflects documented transportation and health‑literacy barriers.

critical_findings_addressed: Stage 2 hypertension (151/105 mmHg) – addressed by multiple hypertension‑related diagnoses
Chronic axial pain – addressed by degenerative spine disease and axial spondyloarthritis
Psychosocial stressors – addressed by depression/PTSD diagnosis
critical_findings_missed: Missing renal function labs (creatinine, eGFR, electrolytes, urine ACR)
No sleep‑apnea screening results (STOP‑BANG, BMI, neck circumference)
top_concerns: Overestimation of metabolic syndrome despite no supporting data
Absence of a focused secondary‑hypertension work‑up (renin‑aldosterone, renal imaging)
Critical laboratory gaps that prevent confirmation or exclusion of key diagnoses
review_summary: The differential is broad and includes most relevant possibilities, but the weighting is misaligned: the most likely cause—poor adherence or inadequate therapy—is under‑prioritized, while metabolic syndrome is over‑emphasized without any data. Key secondary‑hypertension investigations and basic labs are missing, limiting the ability to confirm or exclude several diagnoses. Re‑prioritizing toward adherence assessment and a systematic secondary‑hypertension work‑up is essential.
